chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

About three people who were traveling: one of them was junub, the second was dead, and the third was without wudu (ablution). The time of salat (prayer) arrived, and they had with them only enough water for one of them. Who should take the water, and what should they do?

He said: 'The junub should perform ghusl (ritual bath), the deceased should be buried with tayammum, and the one who is without wudu (ablution) should perform tayammum, because ghusl from janabah is an obligation, washing the deceased is sunnah, and tayammum for the other is permissible.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: The prescribed salat (prayer) whose time has entered.
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: The state of major ritual impurity necessitating ghusl.
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: Ritual washing, here specifically ghusl from janabah.
key_terms.بِتَيَمُّمٍ: By tayammum, dry ablution used in place of water-based purification.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl.
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: Ritual ablution required for salat (prayer) in ordinary circumstances.

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for one person, should it be used for ghusl of a junub, washing a deceased person, or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a case of limited water during travel involving janabah, a deceased person, and someone lacking wudu (ablution). It prioritizes the obligatory ghusl of the junub, permits tayammum for the person without wudu, and treats the washing of the deceased as secondary in this situation.
